MongoDB faces lower expectations ahead of earnings as Bank of America cuts price target Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

MongoDB Inc (NASDAQ:MDB) faces a lower bar for growth when it reports third-quarter financial year 2027 results on December 1, with Bank of America (BofA) warning that concerns about execution have reduced expectations for its Atlas cloud database business.

The brokerage reiterated its 'buy' rating but cut its price objective to $450 from $540, reflecting a decline in valuation multiples across infrastructure software companies.

BofA believes Atlas revenue growth of 29% year-on-year would now be sufficient to meet investor expectations, maintaining the previous quarter's growth rate despite a slightly tougher comparison.

The analysts said recent management changes had increased uncertainty around sales execution and enterprise customer expansion, although they viewed these as execution risks rather than evidence of weakening competitiveness.

Investors will also assess MongoDB's acquisition of Firebolt, announced on November 17, which adds a real-time online analytical processing database to its existing operational database platform.

The bank sees the deal as strategically important for MongoDB's ambition to become a broader AI data platform, potentially expanding the workloads it can address and bringing it into closer competition with Snowflake and privately held Databricks.

Learn more about MongoDB

Read more about MongoDB

The brokerage estimates the artificial intelligence data platform market could reach $495 billion by 2030 and wants management to explain how Firebolt will expand MongoDB's addressable workloads.

Other indicators to watch include annual recurring revenue growth, large-deal activity, enterprise customer additions and sales productivity.

BofA said fourth-quarter Atlas revenue guidance of 26%, in line with its existing outlook, would support the expected growth recovery, while a weaker forecast could delay the investment case.

The brokerage lowered its valuation multiple to 9.9 times calendar 2027 estimated revenue from 12 times.

Roblox shares face near-term pressure as Bank of America maintains 'neutral' rating Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Roblox Corp (NYSE:RBLX) has an improving growth outlook for 2027 as artificial intelligence (AI) accelerates game development, but Bank of America (BofA) has maintained its 'neutral' rating, advising investors to wait for the impact of Grand Theft Auto 6 to become clearer.

The brokerage said the balance of risks for calendar 2027 had improved over the past six weeks, with game launches accelerating as creators increasingly adopt AI tools, potentially supported by Claude's Model Context Protocol integration.

Its discussions with Roblox investor relations and industry experts suggest AI could shorten development cycles, reduce production costs and create opportunities for unexpected revenue growth next year.

One industry expert cited by the brokerage said some AI tools could reduce development costs to almost zero and roughly quadruple the potential rate of game releases.

The number of games on Roblox in November to date was 50% higher than in June, while new launches among the platform's top 100 games reached a record in October, almost 40% above the 2025 summer peak.

Learn about Roblox

Read about Roblox

However, the bank estimates Grand Theft Auto 6 could reduce Roblox engagement hours by about 2% in the fourth quarter, creating a 4.5% headwind to bookings.

The impact is expected to be concentrated in the first two weeks after the November 19 launch, although players could take about six weeks to complete the story mode.

The brokerage cut its fourth-quarter bookings estimate to $1.90 billion from $1.95 billion and EBITDA to $327 million from $356 million.

It raised its price objective to $48 from a valuation multiple of 20 times to 21 times calendar 2027 EBITDA, but said investors should wait for the GTA 6 impact to settle.

title: Is A Fed Hike Still Good News For JPMorgan?
detail:
Is A Fed Hike Still Good News For JPMorgan?
Trefis Team

^GSPC
KRE
XLF
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase

Today's big story: Could Anthropic Stock Fall 25%?

Most investors expect a Fed rate hike to be good news for big banks like JPMorgan Chase. Higher rates let a bank charge more on its loans. On our data, that still holds for the business. It does not hold for the stock.

The short answer is no. Over 21 Fed hikes since June 2006, a fund of big financial stocks beat the S&P 500 in the next three months only 6 times. JPMorgan beat it after 8 of them. Since the latest hike, JPMorgan has lagged the S&P 500 so far, while that fund has beaten it.

How have bank stocks done since the September hike?

The Fed's rise in the top of its target range to 4.0% took effect on Sept 17, 2026. It was its first increase since the one that took effect on July 27, 2023. From the close the day before through Wednesday's close, JPMorgan returned -6.6%, counting dividends. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF, called SPY, returned -2.9%.

Two other big banks did worse. Bank of America returned -15.5% and Citigroup -11.3%. Wells Fargo returned -6.5%, about the same as JPMorgan. Our data shows no single confirmed cause for these drops.

JPMorgan has lost 6.6%, counting dividends, since the Fed hike that many owners expected to help it. If JPMorgan is a big part of your savings, that is a fall you have had to sit through. When the market has fallen, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio has lost about 81 cents for every $1 its benchmark lost, on average. See the HQ record.

Did bank stocks ever rise and fall with rates?

They did, day to day. We measured how closely each stock's daily move tracked the daily change in the 2-year Treasury yield. That yield follows where traders expect Fed rates to go. The measure is called correlation. A high positive score means the two moved together, and a score near zero means no link.

From 2016 to 2019, the yearly score of the Financial Select Sector SPDR fund (XLF) averaged 0.52. JPMorgan's averaged 0.51. In 2026 so far, XLF's score is -0.09 and JPMorgan's is -0.04. The SPDR S&P Regional Banking ETF (KRE), a fund of smaller banks, is at -0.19.

Put simply, bank stocks no longer rise on days when rate expectations rise. SPY now has a negative score too, at -0.13. We think higher yields are trading as bad news for stocks in general.

A $2.6 Billion Fund Dumps These 3 Stocks ©PeterPhoto from Getty Images Signature, Warchi from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

Azora Capital, which manages $2.6 billion, sold all its Bank of America, State Street and Huntington Bancshares shares in the third quarter, its latest 13F shows.

In the same quarter, it opened a new position in First Horizon, now its second-largest holding, and added 30% to its SLM stake.

Analysts' average targets sit 28% above Bank of America's price, 26% above Huntington's and 17% above State Street's.

Bank of America is the one I'd buy back. Its consensus target is higher than a year ago, and Huntington's is lower.

Azora Capital is out of three bank stocks, and three months earlier one of them made up 10% of its 13F stocks. The fund's 13F for the quarter ended Sept. 30, filed Nov. 16, shows no shares left of Bank of America (BAC:NYSE), State Street (STT:NYSE) or Huntington Bancshares (HBAN:NASDAQ).

The buys were lenders too

At June 30, Azora held 4.18 million Bank of America shares worth $238 million, or 10.0% of its 13F stocks. Its State Street stake was 406,286 shares worth $69 million (2.9%), and its Huntington stake was 3.57 million shares worth $63 million (2.7%).

Its buys in the quarter were financials too. Azora opened a new position in First Horizon (FHN:NYSE): 8.33 million shares worth $192 million at Sept. 30. That's 7.3% of its 13F stocks and its second-largest holding. It also added 30% to its SLM (SLM:NASDAQ) stake, which ended the quarter at 4.90 million shares worth $111 million, or 4.2% of its 13F stocks.

A 13F shows only what a fund held on the quarter's last day. It doesn't say when Azora sold or what it got for its shares.

TIKR tracks 25 analysts on Bank of America. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Bank of America, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Bank of America's Analyst Ratings

Bank of America still has the Street on its side

Bank of America is down 14% since Sept. 30 and is 25% below its 52-week high. Its third quarter was mixed. Net interest income rose 8% to $16.4 billion, but fixed-income trading revenue fell 17%. After a $1.2 billion penalty over its money-laundering controls, its return on tangible common equity was 12.6%, or 15% without the penalty. That's down from 17.0% in the second quarter.

Management still guides net interest income up about 8% this year and 8% or more in 2027. Analysts cut their normalized EPS estimates for 2026 to 2028 by 1.4% to 2.4% after the report, which leaves $5.19 for 2027. At Sept. 30, the stock traded at 1.84x tangible book value, above its 10-year average of 1.59x. After the 14% drop since then, it's much closer to that average.

Leverage has cut far deeper into the fund built to double Tesla's (NASDAQ:TSLA) daily moves than into the automaker's own stock in 2026. Direxion Daily TSLA Bull 2X ETF (NASDAQ:TSLL) shares are trading at $9.89 midday on Thursday, down 1.1%. The fund is down 50.46% year to date (YTD).

Shutterstock

Tesla stock is at $381.45, down 16.11% YTD, and it's slipping alongside the fund. SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX), the other public company tied to Tesla CEO Elon Musk, is trading at $140. SPCX shares are down 7% over the past month.

TSLA Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.

The bigger question for the Direxion fund is what it would take to get back to $20. It finished 2025 at $18.67 and last traded above $20 in August 2022, at $20.39.

How Daily Resets Turned Tesla's Slide Into a Deeper Loss

Direxion's fund seeks twice Tesla's return each day, then resets its leverage before the next session. Across weeks and months, each gain or loss compounds on a new base, so the fund's return can drift far from twice what Tesla delivered.

Volatile, sideways trading widens that drift, a drag known as volatility decay. When Tesla swings down and then back up, the fund loses more on the drops than it recovers on the rebounds, and volatility decay helps explain why the ETF has fallen far more than twice Tesla's YTD loss would suggest. A return to $20 would need a strong, steady Tesla rally, and a volatile path could leave the fund behind even if Tesla stock ends higher.

Chicago, IL – November 19, 2026 – Zacks Equity Research shares Dell Technologies DELL as the Bull of the Day and DraftKings DKNG as the Bear of the Day. In addition, Zacks Equity Research provides analysis on JPMorgan JPM, Bank of America BAC and Citigroup C.

Here is a synopsis of all five stocks:

Bull of the Day:

Dell Technologies is aZacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) that builds the servers, storage, networking gear and PCs behind enterprise computing. The company has become one of the largest suppliers of AI server infrastructure in the world.

The AI trade has lost a lot of air this fall, and with that, DELL has been pulled down to levels not seen since June. Even so, the earnings, the guidance and the estimates all still point higher.

All the negative sentiment over the last month has given long-term investors a chance to buy the AI build-out at a discount.

About the Company

Dell is headquartered in Round Rock, Texas, and was founded in 1984.

The company runs two main segments:

- Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) covers servers, storage and networking.

-Client Solutions Group (CSG) covers commercial and consumer PCs.

Dell now gets most of its revenue from ISG, and that segment is growing fastest. AI servers built on the latest GPU platforms are driving that shift, along with a long refresh cycle for traditional servers.

The company is currently valued at $205 billion and has a forward PE of 12. The stock has Zacks Style Scores of "C" in Value, "B" in Growth, and "D" in Momentum.

The AI Bubble Lets Out Some Air

There's no sugarcoating it: AI stocks have had a rough stretch.

NVIDIA has led the space lower, and investors have been selling anything tied to AI hardware first and asking questions later. Dell is down almost 50% from its September high.

The selling assumes the AI spending cycle is peaking. The demand data from Dell's most recent quarter questions that bearish narrative.

Earnings Beat and Raised Guidance

On September 1, Dell reported EPS of $7.04, crushing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.95 by 42%. Revenues reached a record $47.0 billion, topping the $45.3 billion consensus.

Growth was broad-based with ISG revenue surging 89% y/y to $31.8 billion, led by a 122% jump in traditional servers and networking.  CSG revenue climbed 20% to $15.0 billion. Non-GAAP operating income more than doubled to $5.93 billion.

AI demand was the biggest driver as Dell booked a record $60.9 billion in AI orders and ended the quarter with a record $95 billion backlog. Management noted that its pipeline remains a multiple of that backlog, following $131.7 billion in orders over the past 12 months. Dell's AI customer base has also surpassed 6,500.
